title: Why Netflix Fired Dan Lin (and the Truth About His Tension With Greta Gerwig Over ‘Narnia’)
content:
ByMatt Donnelly

Chief Correspondent

“Everyone is collateral damage.”That’s how one topNetflixinsider summarized another bloody Monday at the streamer, which sawDan Linousted as the company’s head of film.Following last week’s 6% workforce reduction at Netflix – which claimed victims including chief content officer Bela Bajaria and Lin’s right-hand Doug Belgrad – consensus said it was a matter of time before co-CEOTed Sarandoswould show Lin the door.It took a day. On the heels of the Bajaria news on Thursday, Sarandos rang Lin on Friday to tell him he’d been dismissed, three sources toldVariety. The exec kept his head up and pressed on through the weekend, appearing at Saturday’s Academy Gala (in the same room as Sarandos) and at a Sunday tastemaker screening to support the filmmakers of “La Bola Negra.” As has been summarized in many articles about the Netflix purge, creative leadership at the company is being overhauled amid poor stock performance and declining user engagement on the platform. Peter Rice, the veteran film and TV executive, will now preside over and shake up the platform’s content.Competing narratives are flying aboutwhyLin was let go, but they arrive at the same conclusion: In the end, it wasn’t working. This, despite Lin meeting his mandates to curb spending and make movies that resonated with subscribers. In firing Lin and Bajaria and ushering in Rice, some say Sarandos was desperate to sell a story about growth to Wall Street (Netflix’s quarterly earnings report drops Tuesday). Others say Lin could not dance fast enough to find the balance between sticky streaming titles and theatrical release experiments (in fairness, he made it halfway through a five-year deal, barely enough time to get a casting announcement together by today’s standards). There are also some interesting leaks around tension he’s said to have with A-list filmmakers like Greta Gerwig and Ben Affleck, which we’ll get to.The Lin era at Netflix was framed around austerity, both by the town and in some ways by “The Lego Movie” producer himself. A June profile in the New York Times declared Lin was done “coddling” Hollywood, bragging he did not “fawn over stars or write blank checks.” The implication was that his predecessor Scott Stuber had overpaid for talent and too-ambitiously committed to a new Netflix movie release every week in 2022. Those efforts scaled back gradually until Stuber exited in mid-2024.Lin entered with a red pen and a machete, the lore goes, in hopes of emphasizing quality over quantity. Some find it convenient that Stuber’s legacy is still being kicked up, perhaps to provide cloud cover for decisions made by Lin and his former boss Bajaria. Amid the noise of the current Netflix layoffs, it’s important to remember that the prevailing logic at Netflix for a long, long time was “we don’t give a shit about theatrical,” said one colorful studio source. Releasing movies in theaters was never part of the Netflix business model. Stuber paid premiums to get filmmakers like Martin Scorsese, Alfonso Cuarón and Rian Johnson on the service. He also worked with fervor to make the theatrical exhibitors accept Netflix titles in any capacity. While they refused at the time, individuals familiar with Sarandos said Stuber laid the groundwork for the inevitable – that the only way to create value around movies is to put them in theaters first.Lin brought this logic to fruition in convincing Sarandos that family-driven IP should receive robust, exclusive theatrical windows before moving on to streaming, individuals with knowledge of Lin said. We’ll see the results next year when Gerwig’s “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” and “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory” come to cineplexes.Where Netflix once organized its internal film teams by the budget range of projects they worked on, Lin grouped his executives according to genre expertise. He also moved swiftly to program release windows left empty by Stuber’s exit (“Nonnas,” “Happy Gilmore 2,” “The Thursday Murder Club”). He spent one day of his work week with the Netflix animation team, where he installed Hannah Minghella as a leader. For the core slate, Lin is credited with wooing Alan Ritchson (“War Machine”), Matthew McConaughey and Ben Stiller for upcoming projects.In the weeks before his exit, reports said Lin clashed with filmmaker Affleck (director of the just-released “Animals”) over the use of his AI platform InterPositive. Perhaps more consequentially was a rift with Gerwig this summer over the upcoming “Narnia.” The movie represents a $250 million theatrical-first gamble.Four sources with knowledge of the matter said that, indeed, Lin and Gerwig had a falling out during a Zoom call about the project earlier this year. On a virtual meeting populated by numerous Netflix executives, Lin is said to have been “dismissive” to the director in conversations about the progress of the film. Lin is known in town to be incredibly fair, but at times obtuse in his frankness. Word travelled fast around Netflix that the meeting had gone south, at which point sources said Bajaria called Gerwig’s producer Amy Pascal to smooth things over. Two sources also said that Gerwig’s new, all-powerful CAA agent Bryan Lourd went to Sarandos directly over the faux pas. Lin was subsequently disappeared from the film, all sources concurred, and Belgrad stepped in as the primary Netflix exec overseeing the project (until, of course, he was laid off last week).None of the sources suggested the incident led to Lin’s firing. One Lin defender said he’s never “afraid to talk about how to make a movie better.” Another person familiar with the company said there are any number of filmmakers who could say the same about Lin’s delivery. While it may be juicy to speculate that Gerwig’s follow-up to the game changer “Barbie” could be troubled, don’t forget that the industry doubted that Margot Robbie film right up to opening weekend. “Barbie” grossed $1.44 billion at the worldwide box office and became the highest-earning release in the history of Warner Bros. Pictures.While talk will instantly turn to Lin’s replacement (is it Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy? “Probably,” said one high-placed source), don’t shed too many tears for Lin. He ascended to Netflix from a successful, self-made business in Rideback.“When I took this job, Bela gave me a simple piece of advice: Be yourself,” Lin wrote in a Monday memo obtained byVariety. “You work here because it’s personal. Because of that unspoken pact between your individual passion for movies and the audiences we serve. To them, movies aren’t about business. They’re about feeling something.”
title_zh: 為什麼Netflix解僱了丹·林(Dan Lin)（及他與格蕾塔·葛韋格(Greta Gerwig)在《納尼亞傳奇(Narnia)》上的緊張關係真相）
content_zh:
馬特·多納利(Matt Donnelly)  
首席記者

「每個人都是附帶損害。」這是Netflix的一位高層內部人士對該串流平台另一個血腥星期一的總結，當天丹·林(Dan Lin)被罷免為公司的電影部門負責人。在上週Netflix進行了6%的裁員後，受害者包括首席內容官貝拉·巴賈里亞(Bela Bajaria)和林的得力助手道格·貝爾格拉德(Doug Belgrad)，共識認為共同首席執行官泰德·薩蘭多斯(Ted Sarandos)早晚會讓林下台。這花了一天的時間。根據三位消息來源告訴《綜藝》(Variety)，在巴賈里亞的消息傳出後，薩蘭多斯在星期五打電話告訴林他已被解雇。這位高層保持著冷靜，並在週末繼續工作，出席了星期六的學院晚會（與薩蘭多斯同在一個房間）和星期日的品味放映會，以支持電影《黑球》(La Bola Negra)的製作人。正如許多關於Netflix裁員的文章所總結的，該公司的創意領導層正在進行大規模的改革，原因是股票表現不佳和用戶參與度下降。資深電影和電視高管彼得·賴斯(Peter Rice)將接管並重塑該平台的內容。

關於林為何被解雇的競爭性說法不一，但最終得出的結論是一致的：最終，這樣的安排並不奏效。儘管林滿足了削減開支和製作能引起訂閱者共鳴的電影的要求。解雇林和巴賈里亞，並引入賴斯，有人說薩蘭多斯急於向華爾街講述增長的故事（Netflix的季度財報將於星期二發布）。另一些人則表示林無法迅速找到在吸引觀眾的串流標題和影院發行實驗之間的平衡（公平地說，按照今天的標準，他在五年合約中走了一半的路程，幾乎沒有足夠的時間來達成選角公告）。還有一些有趣的消息透露他與A-list導演如格蕾塔·葛韋格(Greta Gerwig)和本·阿弗萊克(Ben Affleck)之間的緊張關係，我們稍後會提到。

林在Netflix的時代被塑造成一種緊縮的形象，這不僅是外界的看法，也在某種程度上是「樂高大電影」(The Lego Movie)製片人本人的說法。《紐約時報》在六月的一篇專訪中宣稱林不再「溺愛」好萊塢，並自豪地表示他不會「對明星阿諛奉承或開空頭支票」。這暗示著他的前任斯科特·斯圖伯(Scott Stuber)在人才方面支付過高的報酬，並在2022年過於雄心勃勃地承諾每週推出一部新的Netflix電影。這些努力逐漸縮減，直到斯圖伯在2024年中期離職。

據說林帶著紅筆和砍刀進入，希望強調質量而非數量。一些人認為，斯圖伯的遺產仍在被提及，或許是為了為林和他前任上司巴賈里亞的決策提供掩護。在當前Netflix裁員的喧囂中，重要的是要記住，Netflix長期以來的主流邏輯是「我們不在乎影院」，一位色彩鮮明的工作室消息來源表示。在影院上映電影從來不是Netflix的商業模式。斯圖伯支付高額費用以讓馬丁·斯科塞斯(Martin Scorsese)、阿方索·卡隆(Alfonso Cuarón)和瑞安·約翰遜(Rian Johnson)等導演加入該服務。他還熱衷於讓影院放映Netflix的作品。雖然當時他們拒絕了，但熟悉薩蘭多斯的人士表示，斯圖伯為不可避免的情況奠定了基礎——創造電影價值的唯一方法是先在影院上映。

林將這一邏輯付諸實踐，說服薩蘭多斯家庭驅動的知識產權應該在轉向串流之前獲得強有力的獨家影院窗口，知情人士表示。我們將在明年看到結果，當葛韋格的《納尼亞：魔法師的侄子》(Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew)和《查理與巧克力工廠》(Charlie and the Chocolate Factory)進入影院時。

在Netflix曾經根據項目預算範圍組織內部電影團隊的情況下，林則根據類型專業知識對他的高管進行分組。他還迅速填補了斯圖伯離職後留下的發行窗口（《奶奶們》(Nonnas)、《快樂吉爾摩2》(Happy Gilmore 2)、《星期四謀殺俱樂部》(The Thursday Murder Club)）。他每週有一天的工作時間與Netflix動畫團隊共事，並任命漢娜·明赫拉(Hannah Minghella)為領導。對於核心片單，林被認為成功吸引了艾倫·里奇森(Alan Ritchson)（《戰爭機器》(War Machine)）、馬修·麥康納(Matthew McConaughey)和本·斯蒂勒(Ben Stiller)參與即將到來的項目。

在他離職前的幾週，有報導稱林與導演本·阿弗萊克在使用他的AI平台InterPositive上發生了衝突。或許更具影響力的是他與葛韋格之間的裂痕，這發生在今年夏天，圍繞即將上映的《納尼亞》。這部電影代表著一項2.5億美元的影院首映賭注。

四位知情人士表示，確實，林和葛韋格在今年早些時候的一次Zoom會議中發生了爭執。在一次由多位Netflix高管參加的虛擬會議上，林在談論電影進展時對導演的表現被認為是「輕視」。林在業內以非常公平著稱，但有時在直言不諱上顯得有些遲鈍。消息迅速在Netflix內部傳開，隨後消息來源表示巴賈里亞打電話給葛韋格的製片人艾米·帕斯卡(Amy Pascal)以緩和局勢。兩位消息來源還表示，葛韋格的新任全能CAA經紀人布萊恩·勞德(Bryan Lourd)直接找到了薩蘭多斯，針對這一失誤。隨後，林被從該電影中刪除，所有消息來源一致表示，貝爾格拉德成為該項目的主要Netflix高管（直到他在上週被裁員）。

沒有任何消息來源暗示這一事件導致了林的解雇。一位林的支持者表示，他從不「害怕談論如何讓電影變得更好」。另一位熟悉公司的人士表示，有很多導演可以對林的表現說同樣的話。雖然猜測葛韋格的《芭比》(Barbie)後續作品可能會遇到麻煩可能很誘人，但不要忘記，業界對瑪格·羅比(Margot Robbie)的電影在開幕周末之前也持懷疑態度。《芭比》在全球票房收入達到14.4億美元，成為華納兄弟影業歷史上最高收入的影片。

雖然關於林的接替者的討論會立刻展開（是邁克·德盧卡(Mike De Luca)和帕姆·阿比(Pam Abdy)嗎？「可能吧，」一位高層消息來源表示），但對林不要流太多眼淚。他是從成功的自創企業Rideback升遷至Netflix的。「當我接受這份工作時，貝拉給了我一個簡單的建議：做自己，」林在一份獲得《綜藝》報導的星期一備忘錄中寫道。「你在這裡工作是因為這是個人化的。因為你對電影的個人熱情與我們所服務的觀眾之間的無形契約。對他們來說，電影不是商業，而是關於感受某種東西。」
summary_zh:
馬特·多納利(Matt Donnelly)  
首席記者

「每個人都是附帶損害。」這是Netflix的一位高層內部人士對該串流平台另一個血腥星期一的總結，當天丹·林(Dan Lin)被罷免為公司的電影部門負責人。
